tasks.prompt:
rg panics when --replace is combined with --multiline for certain patterns and haystacks.

Reproduction:

    printf ' b b b b b b b b\nc\n' > haystack
    rg --multiline --replace=x '(^|[^a-z])((([a-z]+)?)\s)?b(\s([a-z]+)?)($|[^a-z])' haystack

Observed: ripgrep crashes with a panic like "slice index starts at X but ends at Y" (with Y < X) and prints no results. Similar inputs such as " b\nb\nb\nb\nc" do the same. Small changes to the pattern or text (for example replacing the first group with `^`) make the crash go away.

Expected: rg should never panic here. It should print the matching lines with each match replaced by `x`, the same way it handles other patterns.

Hidden files that a parent directory's .ignore file whitelists are not searched when `.` is passed as the search path.

Reproduction:

    cd "$(mktemp -d)"
    mkdir subdir
    echo 'foo text' > subdir/.foo.txt
    printf '!.foo.txt\n' > .ignore
    cd subdir
    rg --files        # prints .foo.txt (correct)
    rg --files .      # prints nothing (wrong)
    rg --files ./     # prints nothing (wrong)
    rg --files ./.    # prints ././.foo.txt (correct)

The same happens with `rg -l text .`. If you run from the parent directory, `rg --files .` correctly lists ./subdir/.foo.txt.

Expected: a hidden file whitelisted by an ancestor's ignore file should be listed or searched whether no path, `.`, `./` or `./.` is given. For example, `rg --files .` inside subdir should print `./.foo.txt`.

`--line-regexp` no longer works together with `--null-data` (a regression since ripgrep 13).

Reproduction:

    printf '%s\0' foo bar hello world | rg --null-data --line-regexp foo

Observed: nothing is printed and the exit status says no match. In ripgrep 13.0.0 this printed `foo`.

Expected: with --null-data, NUL acts as the line terminator, so --line-regexp should match whole NUL-terminated records. The command above should print `foo` (NUL-terminated). Likewise, for a file `haystack` containing "foo\0bar\0quux\0", `rg --null-data --line-regexp bar` should print `haystack:bar\0`.
